summary: US-018: Back-office app shell — staff see the venue list
description:
### US-018: Back-office app shell — staff see the venue list
**As** staff, **I want** a back-office web app where I can see the organizer's venues and their GA capacity, **so that** later slices have a surface to author seat maps on. **Priority:** P2 **Depends on:** —

This is the prefactor slice: it stands up a new back-office web app and its gateway route, de-risking the new-app plumbing (framework, pnpm workspace, OpenAPI codegen, gateway routing, Compose wiring, healthcheck) **separately** from any seat-map domain logic. No seat-map code here — it renders venues that already exist.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A new `web/backoffice` app is added to the pnpm workspace and starts under `docker compose up` with a `/healthz` (or equivalent liveness) that the Compose healthcheck gates on; stack matches an existing precedent (storefront Astro+React **or** scanner React+Vite) — the plan picks one with a one-line rationale.
- [ ] The gateway route table gains a back-office prefix (e.g. `/admin/`) proxying to the new app, added alongside the existing `/api/catalog/` and `/` routes without breaking longest-prefix matching; the storefront catch-all `/` still resolves.
- [ ] Catalog exposes a venue **read** the back-office consumes: `GET /venues` (list) and/or `GET /venues/{id}` returning at least `{id, name, ga_capacity}`, `organizer_id`-scoped, with an ADR-004 `Cache-Control` tier declared (hours tier — venue geometry is long-lived) and the OpenAPI contract published (ADR-009).
- [ ] The back-office renders the venue list from that endpoint via generated types; opening `/admin/` in a browser shows the seeded organizer's venues with GA capacity (screenshot in the PR).
- [ ] The M1 storefront and scanner paths are untouched (their smoke tests stay green).

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + unit + integration + smoke; mirrors CI)
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary (ADR-009 drift check)
- New/changed public read endpoints declare an ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale
- New migrations run out-of-band via the service `migrate` subcommand (ADR-022) and build within the 30s startup budget with plain `CREATE INDEX` (ADR-020)
- Every owned entity is `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002)

Parent epic: TKT-3. Full lineage: docs/product/prd-v1.md §Capability map (TKT-3).

binding.rule: Every public read endpoint declares a volatility-tiered `Cache-Control`/`s-maxage`. Venue/seat-map geometry is the 'hours' tier (longer-lived than the 'minutes' event tier); availability is 'seconds'; hold/order state is never cached. Writes are never cached.
Every owned entity carries an `organizer_id` (tenant-aware) even though v1 has one organizer.

governingAdrs.why: The new venue read must declare the 'hours' geometry TTL tier, not the events 'minutes' tier.
Storefront-shell precedent (Astro) — reuse its scaffolding shape if the plan picks Astro; scanner is the React+Vite alternative.
Contract-first: the new venue GET is an OpenAPI addition, codegen'd into the back-office types.
Venue reads and the app are organizer-scoped from birth.
